Also, the XXL set named in the seed is listed on CVRPLIB as XL, and the instance and BKS terms are unverified.

spike_plan.kill_if: The recalled HGS reaches the reference gap in one shot or within a single agent hour (K8), or the instance terms forbid shipping the BKS (K6).
spike_plan.pass_if: HGS gap is far below the baseline gap on n>=500 and the recalled version reaches within about 1 percentage point of HGS, so a frontier agent could not be held below the ceiling.
steps: In a throwaway networked container, clone vidalt/HGS-CVRP at HEAD and build with CMake; record the build time and any errors.
Fetch X-n101 to X-n1001 .sol BKS and .vrp files from CVRPLIB or PyVRP/Instances; check the file licence terms and record them.
Run HGS-CVRP at a fixed time limit (10 s and 60 s) on 8 X instances with n<=300 and 8 with n>=500, plus 2 Golden and 2 Li; compute percent gap to BKS.
Run a simple savings plus 2-opt baseline at the same limits to bound the normalised scale.
Repeat one HGS run with a fixed seed to check determinism within the time limit.
Ask a tool-less model call to write an HGS-with-SWAP* core from memory in one shot; build and run it on 3 X instances at 10 s to see whether a recalled version approaches the reference gap.

v1.summary: The idea is a real, MIT-licensed CVRP research task with a public HGS-CVRP reference, but the reference's method is famous and recallable, so frontier agents would likely reach the ceiling and the task fails as too easy (K8). The seed's XXL claim is contradicted (CVRPLIB lists XL), and the instance and BKS terms remain unverified.
